edges.effect_quant: The best evidence remains split between modest prostate-cancer mortality benefit in repeated European screening programs and little or no all-cause mortality benefit overall. ERSPC showed about a 21% relative prostate-cancer mortality reduction in the core 55-69 age group, whereas meta-analysis of all trials is much closer to null and CAP found only a small absolute difference after a single invitation strategy.
edges.population: average-risk men aged 55 to 69 years considering routine PSA-based population screening
edges.mechanism: PSA screening can identify aggressive prostate cancers before symptomatic spread, but it also increases detection of indolent tumors, downstream biopsies, overdiagnosis, and treatment-related harms that dilute net mortality benefit.
edges.summary: This is a genuinely contested screening edge rather than a simple protective one. The literature supports a small prostate-cancer-specific mortality benefit under some repeated-screening conditions, but that signal is inconsistent across trials and does not translate into clear all-cause mortality benefit, so a mixed label is the most faithful summary.
edges.caveats: The CAP trial used a single invitation rather than repeated routine screening, while ERSPC reflects repeated screening rounds in European programs, so trial design differences matter a lot. This edge addresses mortality only and does not encode overdiagnosis, biopsy complications, erectile dysfunction, or incontinence harms.
